subtopics.title: VAT: the Fifteen Percent on Almost Everything

questions.question: A microwave priced at R240 excluding VAT sells, with VAT at 15%, for:
To remove VAT from a VAT-inclusive price of R276, the correct move is:
Taking 15% off R276 instead of dividing by 1,15 gives R234,60, which is wrong because:
options: It takes 15% of the bigger, already-taxed number
VAT can never be removed from a price

questions.question: Which list contains only zero-rated items?
options: Brown bread, maize meal, fresh vegetables, eggs, milk

subtopics.title: UIF: One Percent from Each Side

questions.question: The UIF deduction on a gross salary of R8 400 is:
The total that reaches the fund each month for that worker is:
options: R168 — 1% from the worker and 1% from the employer

questions.question: UIF is calculated on:
With gross pay of R8 400, UIF of R84 and other deductions of R516, net pay is:

subtopics.title: Exchange Rates: the Price of the Rand

questions.question: At R18,50 per US dollar, a visa fee of $120 costs:
At the same rate, R5 000 converts to:
If the rate moves from R18,50 to R19,20 per dollar, the rand has:
options: Strengthened, because the number went up
Weakened — each dollar now costs more rand

questions.question: A weaker rand is GOOD news for:
options: A family filling up with petrol
A family receiving £400 from a relative in London

subtopics.title: Tariff Systems: Which Option Is Cheaper for You

questions.question: Option A charges R99 per month plus R0,75 per minute. Its cost formula is:
At 200 minutes, Option A (R99 + R0,75/min) against Option B (R1,45/min) gives:
options: A: R249, B: R290 — B wins
A: R249, B: R290 — A wins
A: R174, B: R145 — B wins
A: R290, B: R249 — B wins

questions.question: The crossing point of the two options is found by:
options: Choosing the option with the smaller monthly charge
Setting 99 + 0,75 × m equal to 1,45 × m, giving about 141 minutes

questions.question: On a graph of the two options, the break-even point of the comparison appears as:
options: The steepest section of either line
The point where Option B crosses the vertical axis
The point where Option A starts
The point where the two cost lines intersect

subtopics.title: The Tax Inside the Till Slip

questions.question: The one-move shortcut for adding 15% VAT to a price is:
Adding 15% to a price and then taking 15% off the result:
options: Returns you exactly to the original price
Does not return you home, because the second 15% is taken of a bigger number

questions.question: On a till slip mixing taxable and zero-rated items, VAT is calculated:
options: Only on the taxable lines, leaving the zero-rated basket alone

subtopics.title: The Two R84s on the Payslip

questions.question: The no-calculator way to find 1% of a gross salary is to:
options: Slide the comma two places — R8 400 becomes R84

questions.question: Asked 'how much does the worker contribute to UIF?' when gross pay is R8 400, the answer is:
options: R84 — the employer's R84 never touches the payslip

questions.question: The payslip identity that always holds is:
UIF exists so that:
options: The government collects VAT on wages
Workers pay for their own pensions
A retrenched worker receives a temporary income while looking for work

subtopics.title: Rands Abroad and the Cheaper Phone Deal

questions.question: Thinking of a dollar as an item priced at R18,50, converting R5 000 into dollars means:
options: Asking how many R18,50 items the money buys — divide, about $270

questions.question: When the rand weakens, the cousin's £400 sent home from London:
options: Becomes more rand — bad at the petrol pump, good for the receiving family
Stays exactly the same in rand

questions.question: The general rule for tariff comparisons is:
options: The option with no monthly charge is always cheaper
The option with the fixed charge is always cheaper
Fixed-charge options suit heavy users; pay-as-you-go suits light users; they trade places at the crossing point
Both options always cost the same at 100 minutes

questions.question: The best final answer to a two-option tariff question is:
options: At 100 minutes a month, choose B and save R29
